page: Vultr voc-c-4c-8gb-75s-amd is an instance in the Optimized Cloud Compute family, powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor. The configuration provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware profile is completed by 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB per core, and 75 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No GPU resources are included with this server type.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing the instance in the top 10% of its class. Single-threaded operations, including gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench text processing, show strong performance in the top 25%. However, multi-threaded scaling is more limited; multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng and Geekbench falls into the average category, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is weak, placing in the bottom 25%.

Memory bandwidth for large block writes is strong, though read-only bandwidth remains average. The instance exhibits weak performance in database operations and static web serving throughput, both scoring in the bottom 25%. LLM inference speeds are average for small 135M models but drop to poor or weak for medium 7B models. Given the 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, this instance is suited for compute-focused workloads that rely heavily on single-core execution speed, such as lightweight software compilation, text processing, and single-threaded data processing.
